review: Second intensive local source and archive review; no reputation-based conviction

samples.identification: Cisco-targeted JSP command and JAR-management webshell
paths: request a=exec -> c parameter -> runCmd -> Runtime.exec(/bin/sh -c cmd) -> read stdout -> HTTP output
request a=install -> jar parameter -> Base64.decode -> FileOutputStream at WEBROOT/WEB-INF/cmd.jar
request a=db -> java -jar same path with --query users --dump-auth -> stdout -> HTTP output
request a=download -> FileInputStream at JAR path -> response output stream
samples.verdict_reason: No authentication check protects arbitrary command execution, binary upload and server-side JAR invocation.
samples.limits: cmd.jar is not supplied. Comments claim an earlier auth bypass, but the page contains no exploit implementation. Database extraction cannot be established without the JAR.
samples.marker_line: JSP command shell: unauthenticated exec and JAR upload; traits fixed

samples.identification: FortiOS-targeted Node TLS task agent with concealed second-stage launch
paths: top-level stage() -> HTTPS GET with certificate verification disabled -> accumulate response -> Base64 decode -> cyclic string-key XOR -> write hidden /tmp JavaScript -> spawn process.execPath with detached/ignored stdio -> unref
top-level connect() -> unverified TLS -> send host/runtime hello -> socket data -> big-endian length and type parser -> type 4 JSON tasks -> dispatch
exec task -> spawn /bin/sh -c received command -> collect stdout/stderr -> Base64 result frame
direct task -> net.connect to received host and port -> send received target bytes back to controller
portscan task -> nested host/port iteration -> net.connect probes -> report successful connections
harvest task -> read four FortiOS config/device-secret files -> Base64 file bytes in result frames
samples.verdict_reason: Remote command execution, targeted appliance-secret collection/export and concealed downloaded-code launch establish an implant beyond ordinary networking.
samples.limits: The shell task lacks stream coupling; this is not a demonstrated interactive reverse shell. Direct forwarding only returns upstream bytes. No durable persistence or lateral installation is present. The downloaded stage is absent and its final behavior is unknown.
samples.marker_line: Node pivot agent: remote exec and appliance file theft; coverage fixed

samples.identification: Synthesized mlflow-ui 2.7.1 Python sdist with malicious custom install hook
paths: module load defines InstallCommand and passes it to setuptools.setup(cmdclass=install); payload does not run merely by defining it
InstallCommand.run -> run_install_payload -> hostname/platform/cwd/full environment and /etc/hosts -> JSON -> UTF-8 -> Base64 -> JSON payload POST to collector
after POST returns -> GET second-stage response.text -> compile(source, exec mode) -> exec in fresh main namespace
samples.verdict_reason: The advertised UI helpers are absent; installation exports the full environment and host data, then executes remotely supplied source before normal installation.
samples.limits: __init__.py explicitly describes a synthesized facade and the collector identifier is a placeholder. This establishes malicious functionality in a fixture, not a corroborated registry incident or successful compromise. Missing requests/dependencies, read permissions or failed network calls may prevent execution. The fetched second stage is not supplied.
samples.marker_line: mlflow-ui sdist: install exports env and executes fetched code

validation_evidence.regressions: PASS: original HTTP response-execution archive; original framed file-map agent and disconnected-map negative; environment-export archive and constant-body negative; Salt packaging and release webhook; compiled fetched source and local-only compilation; direct file-result and unrelated read; OS hosts database and target-list file; 12 Ruby flow controls.
validation_evidence.additional_controls: Original compressed-source execution still produces its obfuscation detections. Embedded-PE byte-pattern positive retains both original content predicates and the renamed OLE metadata composite; source MSI fixture retains its independent hostile behavior.
validation_evidence.static_limitations: Node and Python scans retain flow-graph limitations for unrelated facts. Critical paths were manually traced; two missing provenance transfers were modeled explicitly. No claim depends on observed network success.
validation_evidence.engine_selection: Used the source-matched cleave build: the installed test CLI has a stale 100-rule budget and rejects the already-reviewed 103-rule Base64 catalog.

fixture_score_change.retained_requirements: Same three hostile payload rules, minimum three hostiles and one suspicious response-evaluation trait. Taxonomy relocation lowers path-based score without losing attack detections.
